crypto.prefs.encryptWhenPossibleHint: New messages and replies are encrypted by default once Meron has a key for every recipient. You can still turn it off per message.
crypto.sources.why.wkd: WKD (Web Key Directory) asks the recipient's own mail domain for the key, at a fixed address on that domain's website. Only whoever runs the domain can publish there, so it's the most trustworthy source. Proton, Posteo, mailbox.org and GnuPG use it.
crypto.sources.why.vks: keys.openpgp.org only publishes a key's address after its owner confirmed it by email, so nobody can upload a key in someone else's name. Thunderbird searches it by default.
crypto.problem.key_revoked: Signed with a key that {sender} has revoked. The signature doesn't count: the key may have been stolen.
crypto.problem.key_expired: Signed with {sender}'s key after it expired. The signature doesn't count.
